transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Meridian Head of ML), Ethan Morales (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary (auto): POC scoping call for open-model shortlist. Discussed success metrics, latency and cost tradeoffs, multilingual needs (EN/ES/FR + clinical jargon), timeline for benchmarks and next steps.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, with Jules who's our SE. How's everyone?
00:07 Laura: Hi Samir, hi Jules, Laura here. We have about 45 minutes, thanks for squeezing us in.
00:12 Jules: Great, we'll go over the POC scope, shortlist models, sizing and benchmarks and then nail down next steps.
00:20 Priya: Quick note, timeline is kinda tight for us, leadership wants initial results within three weeks if possible.
00:27 Samir: Noted, we'll try to map realistic runs. Jules, can you give a short framing?
00:32 Jules: Sure. The ask as I understand: Meridian wants a POC for clinical note summarization and extraction, multilingual (English, Spanish, French) with domain-specific accuracy. Success criteria we want to define numerically — eg ROUGE / EM-like metrics, plus human QA pass rate. Latency target is sub-350ms p95 for single-turn summarization, throughput ~20 rps average during batch testing. Cost target is, uh, we'd like to keep inference token cost under a rough threshold, we can model that after we pick quantization and model size.
01:05 Ethan: 350ms p95 seems aggressive for larger models, is that for hosted or dedicated? We plan to run initially on our cloud but are open to Redwood Dedicated if needed.
01:14 Jules: Good point. For hosted small-medium models we can often hit ~200-400ms depending on sequence length and quantization. For 7B-class open models, 200-300ms p95 on A100-ish is feasible. For 13B+ you might need dedicated infra or accept higher latency.
01:30 Laura: Our priority is accuracy on clinical abbreviations and preserving PHI-handling. We also need audit logs and KMS integration.
01:37 Samir: We will include SOC 2 and KMS notes in the security packet. For PHI, we recommend Private deployment for later stages, but for POC hosted with strict logging and deletion policies can work.
01:48 Priya: Great. Model shortlist? We're biased toward open models for cost and auditability.
01:53 Jules: Here's a pragmatic shortlist — Llama 2 13B (fine-tune or instruction-tuned variants), Mistral 7B Instruct, Falcon 7B/40B options for domain adaptation, RedPajama-INCITE 7B and 3B for faster runs, and MosaicML MPT variants. Also consider open instruction-tuned models like OpenAssistant derivatives. Tradeoffs: 7B models are cheaper and faster but may need instruction-tuning or LoRA to hit clinical accuracy. 13B and 40B give better out-of-box quality but higher latency and cost.
02:36 Laura: Are there multilingual models in that list that support Spanish/French well?
02:39 Jules: Llama 2 has decent multilingual coverage; Mistral is more English-focused. Falcon and some RedPajama variants vary; for Spanish/French we might use a mix — main model for English plus a smaller localized model or do a single multi-lang variant like Llama 2 13B if latency budget allows. We can also fine-tune on a small Spanish clinical corpus.
02:58 Ethan: For benchmarks, what inputs do you need? Sequence lengths? tokenization?
03:02 Jules: Ideally: 5k representative examples, average input length, typical output length, and a few worst-case long sequences. Provide language split and priority intents (summarization vs extraction). We'll run quality (ROUGE, exact match for entities) and latency/throughput with realistic batching.
03:19 Samir: For the POC we recommend three model flavors: fast (7B quantized int8), balanced (13B q4/LoRA), and high-quality (30-40B on dedicated). That frames cost/latency tradeoffs in the benchmark.
03:33 Laura: That sounds reasonable. Our success criteria: >85% human QA acceptance on summaries, entity extraction F1 > 92, latency p95 < 350ms for balanced use case, and cost per 1k requests under the ballpark — can you give a sample cost model?
03:49 Samir: We'll include a sample cost model with assumed infra and token lengths. It's an estimate but helps leadership.
03:54 Priya: Timeline — you said we can run initial tests in about a week?
03:58 Jules: We need the dataset and credentials. Once we have the samples, provisioning the POC namespace and installing the models takes ~48 hours. Then run baseline quality + latency tests which take 2-3 days. So week-of-Nov-10 for initial results fits.
04:18 Ethan: Any recommended quantization guides? We need to know if int4 is safe for clinical accuracy.
04:22 Jules: Int8/q4f16 is a good starting point. Int4 can save cost but sometimes hurts hallucination/precision. For extraction tasks, we prefer q4 variants plus LoRA fine-tunes. We can run comparative QA in the benchmark.
04:36 Laura: On security — we need SSO, audit logs, and KMS. Also clarify data residency — some data must stay in EU.
04:45 Samir: Redwood Private supports customer VPC and on-prem for residency. For the POC we can pin region and ensure logs are retained per your policy; I'll send the compliance packet.
04:55 Priya: Competitors — leadership asked how Redwood compares to Anthropic/Anthropic-infer, OpenAI endpoint, and self-hosting.
05:02 Samir: High level: Anthropic/OpenAI have managed endpoints and high-quality models but less flexibility for private deployments. Self-hosting gives control but costs more to operate. Redwood tries to blend a production-grade runtime, routing and cost controls plus private deployment options. We'll include a short competitive note.
05:20 Laura: For model tuning, can Redwood run LoRA on our behalf or do we handle fine-tune?
05:25 Jules: We can run or help with LoRA workflows; for sensitive data it's often safer to run in your environment or in a private deployment. For the POC we can use surrogate fine-tuning on sanitized data and then show the delta.
05:38 Ethan: Benchmarks: what metrics will you provide?
05:40 Jules: Latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps), token cost, quality metrics (ROUGE, BLEU where applicable, entity F1), and human QA samples. We'll also show cost per 1k responses at different batching/quantization settings.
05:57 Laura: We also want a small scoring harness so our non-ML reviewers can reproduce runs.
06:01 Jules: We'll provide a benchmark harness and a spreadsheet with inputs and expected outputs; Samir will attach the sheet.
06:08 Priya: Anything else re: timeline?
06:10 Samir: Recap of next steps: Samir sends benchmark template, cost model and security docs by Thursday 2025-11-06. Laura sends dataset and success criteria by 2025-11-07. Jules provisions POC cluster and runs initial tests week of 2025-11-10. Follow-up meeting to review results on or around 2025-11-13.
06:27 Laura: That works. Quick question: if we hit accuracy gaps, how do we proceed?
06:30 Jules: We'll iterate LoRA + prompt engineering; if needed upgrade to a larger model on dedicated infra. We'll tie regressions to the evaluation harness so it's measurable.
06:41 Ethan: One more ops question — can Redwood expose tracing and per-token latency breakdowns?
06:47 Jules: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdowns and traces; we'll include sample screenshots in the follow-up.
06:53 Samir: Great. If no more questions, we'll wrap and send notes. Thanks everyone.
06:58 Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
07:01 Laura: Thanks all.

Notes: Transcript has occasional auto-caption errors (model names sometimes mis-typed), filler words kept. References to decks and benchmark spreadsheet — Samir to attach link in follow-up email.
